Smart health, wellness and biomedical engineering

The air is
the safety
system.

An Integrated HVAC Engineering Framework for Cyclotron and Nuclear Medicine Facilities.

Eng. Febous Wambua Njeru, P.E. Faeb Engineering Ltd · Nairobi KUTRRH Integrated Molecular Imaging Centre
IMIC, Kenyatta University Teaching, Referral and Research Hospital · PETtrace 800
The problem

Comfort will not contain this room.

The system has to set the direction of air, hold the source, protect the clean work, and remove the heat.

01
DirectionAir moves toward the hazard on purpose, and that direction is proved with the doors shut.
02
ContainmentThe radioactive source stays in. The clean preparation stays protected from it.
03
ContinuityEquipment heat leaves without stopping a product that cannot be stored.
The requirements already exist. They arrive in pieces. The missing piece is the method that makes them one installation.
Why it is a problem now

The half-life will not wait.

An air or cooling-water failure stops production and takes the day's doses off the board.

93kW
Earlier check, if the electrical input is dumped into the room.
2kW
What the manufacturer actually gives the room air.
65–70kW
Rejected to process water. The water circuit is the heat sink.
What we are proposing

A sequence another engineer can audit.

  1. 01
    Hazard.Name the source and the direction of air before choosing an air-change rate.
  2. 02
    Airflow.Calculate supply, extract and transfer together.
  3. 03
    Heat.Take room gain and water duty from the manufacturer. Do not use the electrical input as the room load.
  4. 04
    Intelligence.Sensors, alarms and trends come after the mechanical requirement. Local interlocks hold the safe state.
  5. 05
    Proof.Qualify it, and let the result write back into maintenance and the next design.
Intelligent monitoring supports the validated design. It does not replace it.
What the proposal looks like

Positive protects.
Negative contains.

Hot laboratoryGrade C · product protection
+30 Pa

−100 Pa
Cyclotron room−20 Pa

Airlock−10 Pa

Sterility+10 Pa

Coordinated schematic setpoints, not a floor plan. NC means the cyclotron and control rooms are not classified. The pressure setpoint still stands. Whole-facility extract exceeds supply by 0.424 m³/s, 14.7%.

Why it is viable

A second engineer can repeat it.

0.413
m³/s supply · 1,488 m³/h · 15 air changes. Calculation-stage cyclotron room.
8.4 K
Water temperature rise at 70 kW and 120 L/min. 6.3 K at 160 L/min.
92%
Independent qualification against GMP, the user requirement, the drawings and WHO guidance.
Balance to the coordinated schedule, 1,312 / 1,655 m³/h. The 92% is substantial compliance. Read it with the test sheets. It is not an energy score.
Why it is the one to adopt

Nothing new has to be bought first.

It starts at the actual mistakeDirection of air, and which system receives the heat, are decided before equipment is sized.
It uses the documents already on the jobLayouts, the airflow schedule, the schematic, PETtrace data, BMS records, and the qualification report.
The safe state stays in the roomLocal interlocks hold if the supervisory network drops. Trends advise until a change is retested.
The example is already qualifiedKUTRRH is a working molecular imaging centre, not a diagram of a smart building.
Variable-speed drives and pressure reset stay inside the airflow and pressure limits already qualified.
The bottleneck

Four ways a correct-looking design still fails.

01
Pressure is not a percentage.−20 Pa depends on leakage area, door seals, and door operation.
02
Two airflow figures exist.The hand check is 1,488 m³/h supply. The schedule to balance is 1,312 / 1,655.
03
There is no year of faults.Energy saving and downtime reduction cannot be quantified from the records in hand.
04
A qualified setpoint is frozen.An algorithm that moves airflow or pressure can break a validated state.
How those are addressed

Prove it in the room. Then leave the algorithm advisory.

  1. 01
    Test the path.Doors closed, airflow at the gaps, and recovery after a door opens.
  2. 02
    Label the figure.The hand check shows the method. Balancing uses the approved schedule.
  3. 03
    Measure before you claim.Energy, alarms, recovery time, and unplanned downtime, before and after any predictive rule.
  4. 04
    Retest any automatic change.Change control, cybersecurity review, and a fallback. Local control holds the safe state without the network.
Duty and standby where a failure would stop safe production. Extract failure alarms and goes to the approved safe state.
What we are proposing

Hazard first. Heat second. Qualify before anything smart.

  1. 01Use this sequence on the next cyclotron or nuclear-medicine HVAC package.
  2. 02Keep KUTRRH as the worked example, and the coordinated schedule as the document that gets balanced.
  3. 03Let monitoring support a design that has already been tested.

Bridging the Academia–Industry Gap in MEP Engineering: a structured mentorship framework.

Eng. Febous Wambua Njeru, P.E. Faeb Engineering Ltd · Nairobi A method for employers, universities, IEK and EBK to test

From a defined problem
to carrying
the problem.

Diagnose · Plan · Practise · Review · Progress
The problem

The gap is not the formula.

It is the moment a defined problem becomes a problem you have to define, coordinate and sign for.

01
The brief is unfinished.The graduate waits for complete inputs instead of naming assumptions and missing data.
02
The number never meets the building.A calculation stops short of equipment, a route, a schedule and a test.
03
The software sounds sure.Output is accepted without a check on inputs, limits or consequences.
A correct calculation still fails the project if it cannot be built, powered, maintained or tested.
Why it is a problem now

Years served is not a competency.

BIM, digital controls, AI-assisted tools and green-building rules are ordinary delivery. Fluency in the tool can hide the missing judgement.

Looks like experience

Years on the drawing only

Proficient in the software. Unclear why the design criterion was chosen.

Also looks like experience

Years on the site only

Fluent in installation. Little evidence of calculations, specifications or a design basis.

What we are proposing

Five moves around one portfolio.

Each move uses a real project task. Supervision lightens only after a recorded decision.

Diagnose. Plan. Practise. Review. Progress. Approval stays with the responsible engineer.
PortfolioEvidence
01Diagnose
02Plan
03Practise
04Review
05Progress
What the proposal asks for

236 litres a second. Then the real work.

Qₒ = (20 × 10) + (120 × 0.30) = 236 L/s

Teaching inputs only: 120 m², 20 people, 10 L/s per person + 0.30 L/s per m², duct velocity held at 5 m/s. Do not reuse the rates without the applicable code.

Nominal circular duct 250 mm Free area 0.0472 m² · diameter 245 mm. This is not the deliverable.
Code referenceNoisePressure lossDiffuserFan dutyRoute and structureFire strategyControls sequenceCommissioning test point
The evidence is the chain: a checked calculation, a coordinated drawing, a schedule and a test.
Why it is viable

Begin smaller than an academy.

01MatrixTwo pages. What is evidenced, and what is missing.
02MentorOne named engineer who can say no.
03QuarterA review that actually happens.
04PortfolioCalculations, drawings, inspections, tests.
It follows the Engineers Board of Kenya path, and the WFEO and International Engineering Alliance graduate attributes. The learning environment is the project the firm already has.
Why it is the one to adopt

Evidence, not attendance.

Levels follow the domainLevel 4 in drafting can sit beside Level 2 in commissioning. Time served does not move the level.
Every rating has a fileA calculation, drawing, bill, inspection or test. The mentor records the decision.
The missing work becomes visibleA dashboard shows repeated design and no procurement, commissioning or handover.
Tools stay inside the ruleNo AI-assisted output is issued until the engineer can reproduce it and sense-check it.
The bottleneck

One career is not a population.

01
No cohort yet.The mechanism is real in one record. It has not been shown to generalise.
02
Mentors will disagree.The same task can be Level 2 in one office and Level 4 in another.
03
Exposure will be uneven.A busy office, or a small firm, may never offer procurement or commissioning.
04
A score can float free.An index can look exact and still point at no file an assessor can open.
The paper claims no gain in employability, and no reduction in project error. Those claims wait.
How those are addressed

Count the pilot, not the biography.

  1. 01
    Competence change.C2 minus C1 on the weighted index, across the agreed domains.
  2. 02
    First-pass acceptance.Submissions accepted before a major correction, over submissions made.
  3. 03
    Closure time.Days to close review comments, over the reviews given.
  4. 04
    Exposure completion.Planned exposures the employer actually gave.
  5. 05
    Independent delivery.Level 4 tasks over the tasks eligible for Level 4.
32.1% to 60.7% is an illustration of the index. It is not a result. One rubric, calibration, and a file behind every score.
What we are proposing

One matrix. One mentor. One quarter. Then a pilot.

Employers, universities, IEK and EBK report the five indicators before anyone claims the gap is closed.
